column11:
I originally made a big comment on my Episode 7 entry here in this list, but I decided to remove it and kind of replace it with this one here, seems like a better place anyway as this is the conclusion. So this new one has both the thoughts I had in the ep 7 note + my final thoughts (A little less rambling and more organized too)

Wow, when I originally read the VN I was completely clueless about things that are made completely obvious in the manga. I'm kinda interested in going back to the VN and finding out if I'm really just extremely slow or if it's really that much more vague. I pretty much didn't get anything after Episode 6 anymore it seems. 

Everything is so clear to me now, I finally get it. I am so glad I "gave another chance" to Umineko by reading the manga - In fact, I kinda pinned my hopes on it after I finished the VN because I really wanted to like it but I just had so many problems with it, turns out I just didn't get a thing. I feel so stupid, I couldn't pick up any undertones in the VN. This adaptation feels like it was made for me specifically lol, it was everything I had hoped it would be.
The manga original content was great too, especially since I didn't understand a certain character at all, like on fundamental level. I had a completely new perspective of this story and could connect way much better with the characters and their motivations.

While this is obviously me saying that I enjoyed the manga way better than the VN, I'm not saying that the VN is bad or anything. I really would have to go back to compare how different it actually is except for the completely original scenes, but I think the reasons why I felt the way I felt about Umineko originally was because I was actually stupid and not even trying to deduce anything on my own. I said that in the comment on Episode 7, I think I kind of tapped out mentally after Episode 6 in the VN and wasn't really processing anything anymore. At some scenes in the manga that were definitely in the VN I could put pieces of the puzzles together on my own and I understood things that I didn't understand at all in the VN.
Maybe I took Will's "Don't try to understand. You'll just get a headache." too seriously lol

I'm sure that regardless of all that, there are probably dozens of things and undertones that I still didn't pick up, but this time I definitely got lots of things out of it (and it got lots of emotional responses out of me...)
I'm very happy that I can now wholeheartedly say that I don't only love Higurashi but Umineko too.

I hope I can say the same thing again in the future...

...When something else cries.

(also please check out the finish date i swear this wasn't intended, i realized two days ago that at my pace i'll very probably finish it on the 5th but that was not planned at all beforehand)

column11:
I don't know what to say... I always say that finishing a slice of life anime feels like losing your family, but this is so much worse than usual...

If you told me last year that I'd become a My Little Pony fan, I actually wouldn't have been extremely surprised, I always thought that people should broaden their horizons and don't shy away from genres etc they're not accustomed to. 
And I believe that that's not just something I only preach, as you can see this list is pretty random. And I'm super glad that I'm following this mindset, since it makes me stumble upon things I come to love so often, which wouldn't be the case if I were a person who limits themselves to only one medium or genre - which is something I see quite often on the net and that always makes me kind of sad.

Before I started Season 1 I didn't really know anything about this series at all. I mean yeah, obviously I've seen some ponies somewhere on the net or like profile pictures and stuff, but I did not know what to expect at all, I only knew that MLP has had a very large cultural impact and I kind of always wanted to know what this was about. So when I noticed that I've been rewatching multiple years old youtube videos for the 100th time in between anime episodes because I never found anything new to watch (I still don't) I thought maybe I could finally check MLP out, since I assumed it'd be very lighthearted and be a perfect palette cleanser between anime episodes or to watch while eating. This kind of didn't work though and I watched it like I would an anime lol

Now I don't really know what happened with Season 3, because it took me multiple months to finally watch the last 2 episodes for some reason. I really can't tell you what happened there, I kinda just got too invested into other things at that time I presume, but I'm glad I did eventually get around to continuing it because it definitely fully clicked after that (as you can clearly see in this list lol)

I can't believe it's already over, I've had so much fun with this series and I don't think I've ever watched anything else that made me smile throughout whole episodes, I swear sometimes my face hurt after an episode. But don't you think for a second we'll grow apart soon my little ponies, because you can bet your flanks I will revisit at least Season 1-3 probably in the very near future because of the big break

This has been the most awesomest and funnest journey ever and I'm actually not done yet, there's still two Equestria Girls movies left + some shorts if I understand it right and then there are doooozens of official comics that I've already downloaded and can't wait to dig into, apparently the later issues of the comics are officially called Season 10
I don't think I've ever read any western comics so reading from left to right might be a little bit of a challenge at first (insert ken-sama image)

Yeah what more can I say? Other than...

...Friendship is Magic.

And Fluttershy best pony and outside mane 6 THE GREAT AND POWERFUL TRIXIE!!!

column7: i'm glad i finally got around to reading it but i do have some things to say (hover)
column11:
it's one of those cases where i can pinpoint multiple things i dislike about it and yet without being able to tell you why exactly i overall enjoyed it very much. i kind of hate it when this happens because it feels like im deceiving myself but that's just what i'm feeling. i wasn't sitting there at any time hoping i would get done with it soon, i was very much invested.

i'm not sure how deep i want to dive into my problems, but the biggest thing definitely is the fighting. this manga is sooo fighty from start to end and there's a pattern i've noticed that happens almost twice in every volume: 4 pages of guts slashing through a bunch of people/monsters followed by 4 reaction panels of background characters going "SUGOIII!! WHO IS THAT MAN?! HOW CAN HE WIELD SUCH A BIG SWORD?!?! I'VE NEVER SEEN ANYTHING LIKE IT!!" and i just got soo tired of this pattern. at times berserk felt worse in that regard than many battle shonen. in fact, i would even say berserk mostly felt to me like a battle shonen with an adult painting on it. 
it's not that i generally hate fights/hype moments and aura - there are lots of battle shonen i like - but it's just not what i really expected from this manga, i do acknowledge that character development often happens through those fights, but still, it was just too much at times. when i was happy the fights finally ended the next one began, zero breathing room. especially when it has another 4 page slashing 4 panels SUGOOOOIII

what i also didn't really like was when whole rpg party shenanigan got introduced, it felt very silly. not really much more i can say about that it just feels very silly every time schierke goes on about her magic stuff. in that regard i'm kinda happy guts just kept slashing through his enemies

then there's puck... i didn't dislike puck at first but oh man... i think a comic relief character works best if they actually have some significance, which puck doesn't. i kept hoping he would play some important part at some point, especially when elfhelm came up, but no. he just doesn't do anything other than making some witty joke in every panel when the group is together. i can guess that this is something many people say and i really wanted to like him but at some point he just got mind-numbing.

i think this is a common thinking but the black swordsman/golden age arc are what carried this manga very much and why i was still feeling so invested. i just really wanted to see how the rivalry of Guts and griffith ties up, most things around it are just okay. not bad but okay. there's not really an arc i particularly disliked or anything. that's also what makes it feel like a battle shonen to me. 

berserk is just way sillier than i expected. since the "dark and gritty" moments are great, the silly battle shonen moments kind of take away a lot from the atmosphere.

well and then there's the elephant in the room, yeah i don't know what to really think about the continuation after miura's death. everything about it feels really off. obviously the art isn't the same but even how the plot progresses, and i'm afraid the latest chapter looks like they're going full battle shonen now. idk it just not the same at all anymore, which was obvious. feels very weird reading a direct continuation while knowing the mangaka isn't behind any of these characters i've known for 300+ chapters anymore. no matter how well they pulled this off, it would always feel weird and like a fanfiction, which it basically is.

as i said in the beginning of this endless rambling, i have lots of issues with berserk. nevertheless i had fun reading it. can't dive deeper into that feeling, it's similar to when i was reading naruto earlier this year. had lots of issues with that one too but i still enjoyed it. sounds very mindless but that's just what i'm feeling.
